The evidence found confirms the year and the names of the initiators, but does not explain in detail what specific purpose the temple was established for. It is therefore better understood as a religious site of a local community taking shape in the Takua Pa basin, rather than tied to stories without direct evidence.

หลังสึนามิวันที่ 26 ธันวาคม 2547 วัดถูกใ: After the tsunami on 26 December 2004 (B.E. 2547), the temple was used to gather victims' remains while awaiting forensic identification. This temporary role made Wat Yan Yao part of Takua Pa's disaster-response history. Later, on 30 October 2022 (B.E. 2565), the Phang Nga Provincial Office of Buddhism jointly presented a land-title document to the abbot, evidence of contemporary land-ownership administration.
